K2.reason: Linux secret_ensure_client_key and Windows Initialize-ClientKeySecret read secret_key_sign_name and key_min_bytes from service_contract.json#client_key_auth. They generate only when the raw file is absent or empty, no <name>.js/.JS encrypted copy exists, and no bundle entry exists. The bundle match string '"filename": "<name>"' is exactly what every bundle writer produces (JSON.stringify(..., null, 2) in bundle_add_file/bundle_encrypt/migrate/remove). Because the checks look at encrypted copies, not at the queued decrypt result, a host that holds an encrypted copy never generates a divergent key. The key is 32 random bytes as base64url, written 0600 via mktemp+mv (Linux) or with an owner/SYSTEM/Administrators ACL (Windows), and is never printed. The existing re-encrypt prompt picks it up.

IS-008.reason: repair_owned_tree_777 prunes .secret_keys, .secrets and .git from the 777 walk for every caller. Secret stores get repair_private_tree (dirs 0700, .secret_ignore/raw files 0600, tracked encrypted copies go-rwx; git tracks only the x bit, so there is no git diff). .git gets chown plus go-w. The decrypt, re-encrypt and generate paths also repair the private tree right away. Runtime readers stay compatible: Octane runs as root, and pyservice drops to the desktop user, which is the permission user that owns the store.

IS-010.reason: All node secret-tool calls on Linux and Windows pass the password on stdin through secret_password_runner.js. The Windows twin of step 27, Step5_InstallGitSSH.ps1:105/:112, now uses Invoke-SecretPasswordTool (GlobalVars.ps1 is dot-sourced at :13) and clears $plainPassword/$plainConfirmPassword on every path. Prompts are hidden (secret_read_hidden, Read-Host -AsSecureString).
